title: The Scorch Protocol, A to Z
subtitle: One path from “am I ready?” down to regeneration.

side.title: STOP, not now
side.body: Pregnant or breastfeeding · type 1 diabetes · active or advanced heart disease · active kidney disease · underweight or an eating disorder, current or past · an active infection · active cancer · under 18.

asks.title: What if I have POTS, type 2 diabetes on medication, or take many medications?
asks.body: Not a no. In Yannick’s experience fasting is still very advisable with POTS. Medications are tapered down as far as possible first, planned with Yannick.

main.title: Take your baseline temperature
main.body: Take a baseline: waking temperature for 7 mornings, before getting out of bed.

asks.title: Do I need lab tests first?
asks.body: No. Labs are good for a baseline if you can get them, but temperature and symptoms are enough to start.

main.title: Cold AND ill for over a year?

side.title: Poorer fit
side.body: Ill with a normal temperature may be a different illness. Cold but otherwise healthy does not need this.

asks.title: Who responds best?
asks.body: People already worn down by years of intermittent fasting, calorie deficits or very long fasts. It helped at first, then the fasts stopped helping and they began to slide. Usually cold, with very low energy.

asks.title: Is simple fasting enough, or do I need all of this?
asks.body: In Yannick’s experience plain fasting resolves a great deal, and most people never need more. Scorch is the advanced version, for the few whose fasting has stopped working.

asks.title: I have been ill for years. Is it too late?
asks.body: The longer it has run, the harder it is to heal. Still possible.

asks.title: Am I too old for this?
asks.body: Almost no age is too old. An older body is weaker and needs a slower build-up, and the early, short fasts will show whether it can handle more.

side.title: No fasting yet
side.body: Below 96.0 °F (35.6 °C): raise the metabolism first (T3 first, set with Yannick).

asks.title: What do the bands mean?
asks.body: 96.0 to 96.9 °F: usually can fast, case by case. 97.0 to 97.7: usually clear. 97.8 and up: ideal. The bands follow Wilson’s protocol and Broda Barnes’s work on low thyroid.

main.title: Years of low carb, stalled and cold?

asks.title: Should I take T3 before my first fast?
I am a woman and my period has stopped. Does that change it?
Can I skip preparation?
asks.body: No. The only near-exception is someone already on a near-carnivore diet, and even then it is not ideal. On many medications, never.

asks.title: Plant-based or keto?
Do I need a liver flush?
What do I write down on day 0?
Can I go straight to five days?
asks.body: Never. The ladder builds tolerance: 36 hours, then 72, then the full fast, with recovery between rungs.

asks.title: How do I know I am ready for the next rung?
How long should I go?
asks.body: Five days dry is the cap at home. Deeper fasts may go further but demand a stricter refeed and more care.

asks.title: Day 3 feels awful. Do I quit?

side.title: A stop rule, or a prodrome
side.body: Stop rule hit: break the fast. Prodrome (tingling, sore throat, low fever): end the dry phase, go to water, sodium kept low, L-lysine at once.

asks.title: Kidney pain?
Why water after dry, not before?
asks.body: The order is locked. Water rehydrates the kidneys before food returns and before any antiviral drug can go in.

asks.title: Why so slow?
asks.body: Refeeding syndrome is real, and days 1 to 14 are the consolidation window: new cells are settling, and any fresh stress can lock them back.

asks.title: How many cycles will I need?
If I stall, should I fast more or deeper?
asks.body: No. A stalled rebuild is not answered with more fasting.

asks.title: Is hGH required?
asks.body: No. It is the last step, only when the body cannot enter regeneration on its own. It is difficult to obtain, so it is not a required step, but it almost always improves the situation when used correctly.

main.title: Regeneration not starting on its own?

asks.title: Who must not use hGH?
asks.body: Anyone with active cancer; every cancer history goes to Yannick first. Screening comes before it.

asks.title: Is the rebuild different for women?
How do I know I am ready?
asks.body: Temperature near normal, a wider energy envelope, quick recovery after effort.
